# Torsion bars and front ride height

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Ensure stock upper control arms work and note that original length shocks may limit suspension travel. [t1849]

[Partial] Crawl under the vehicle to locate and adjust torsion bars for front ride height. [t1138]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Ensure you can use your stock upper control arms for the procedure.
2. Note that using original length shocks may limit suspension travel.

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t1138] [Partial]</summary>

1. Crawl under the vehicle to locate a long bolt sticking upward toward the body on each side of the crossmember.
2. [Partial] Loosen the lock nut while lifting the front of the truck to prevent stripping the adjustment bolt.

</details>

## Parts

- [Partial] Shocks, Original Length: Usable but may limit travel [t1849]
- [Partial] Stock Upper Control Arms: Optional but usable [t1849]

## Tips & gotchas

- Consider upgrading shocks if you want full suspension travel. [t1849]
- [Partial] Stock upper control arms are compatible with the re-indexing process. [t1849]
- [Partial] Lift the vehicle off the ground before adjusting so you can check height easily by setting it back down repeatedly. [t1138]
- Apply oil and use a wire brush on rusted bolts beforehand for easier movement. [t1138]
- Use an air or cordless ratchet to remove the bolt if necessary, but switch to a breaker bar when tightening. [t1138]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Stripping the long adjustment bolt by using too much impact force without lifting the vehicle first, [t1138]
